answer:
Headline results for run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (stride 20):

- Records analysed: 759, covering 2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z (3.314% of the time window).
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57.
- DAS detections: 62 detections in 53 records; relative b = 0.9849 (34 above Mc).
- Pumping: injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days.
- Catalogue: 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07 (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016).

CALIBRATED (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5, LBNL/NCEDC magnitudes — this is the calibrated probability):
  b = 1.0:  Sigma = -5.449, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198, P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume = 5.236e-06, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.03719
  b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.319, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922,  P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume = 0.0002155, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.2809
  b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.281, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474,   P(Mw>=5.5) over observed volume = 0.0006484, P(M>=3)/yr = 0.4653

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at/above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts — this is the DAS-based upper bound, NOT calibrated):
  b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(Mw>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Interpretation: the calibrated LBNL-catalogue estimate puts the annual probability of a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event at 1.2e-4 to 1.5e-2 depending on the b scenario (0.00012 at b=1.0 up to ~0.015 at b=0.65), while the DAS-based upper bound, using uncalibrated DAS magnitudes and counting all 62 detections as events, gives 0.078/yr — roughly 5x higher than even the most pessimistic calibrated scenario, because it over-counts.
